reason: Wrapping the water line with reflective quilt stock seems directly useful for sheltering it from the cold.
expectation: I expect to insulate the water line, though I’m unsure whether it will need further protection.

alternatives.reason: The bricks could help build the cabin’s protective shell, but the water line is the current goal.

effect: The quilt stock insulated the water line, but the sheltering goal remains open.
reaction: That was a straightforward first layer; I’m curious what further protection the line needs.
reason: Using the shovel on the insulated line suggests burying it for additional shelter, which fits the current goal.
expectation: I expect to bury or cover the insulated line, though I’m unsure whether that will complete the goal.

alternatives.reason: The bricks could start the cabin shell, but the water line still needs shelter.

effect: The line is now insulated in a shallow trench with accessible connections, though its heat tracing still needs power. The next goal is to protect the cabin without loading its skin.
reaction: The accessible connections and distinction between slowing heat loss and powering the heat tracing made the result more informative.
reason: The bricks at the cabin perimeter are the only available combination and seem suited to building the protective shell.
expectation: I expect the bricks to form a freestanding wall around the cabin, though I’m unsure whether it will need further work.

effect: The wall stands on its own footing, leaving room for local material without loading the cabin’s pressure shell.
reaction: The separate footing makes the purpose of the wall clear.
reason: The shovel and wall are the only available combination, and the result suggests packing local material against the wall.
expectation: I expect to add local material against the wall to improve the cabin’s shelter, though I’m unsure whether that completes the goal.

effect: The bermed cabin completes the goal of protecting the cabin without loading its skin, and the heater now cycles off.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the shelter have a visible effect while preserving the view from the window.

mostWorthwhile.text: Burying the insulated water line was most worthwhile because it explained how the covering slows heat loss while keeping the connections accessible, and made clear that the heat tracing still needs power.

leastWorthwhile.text: Wrapping the line was straightforward but gave little feedback beyond naming the insulated line; the following trench result was more informative.

surprise.text: I was struck that the insulated line's heat tracing still needed power, and that the wall needed its own footing to keep the packed material from loading the cabin.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: the shovel and bricks had clear roles, although the final two choices were the only combinations offered.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because the practical details about heat loss and structural support made me curious about the next challenge.
